extraFacts.fact: ISO 228-1 specifies pipe threads, designated G, where pressure-tight joints are not made on the threads: both the external and internal thread are parallel (BSPP). The seal is made by a washer, O-ring, bonded seal or sealing face, not by the thread flanks.
ISO 7-1 specifies pipe threads where pressure-tight joints are made on the threads: the external thread is a taper thread (designated R, BSPT) and the internal thread is parallel (Rp) or taper (Rc).

ASME B1.20.1 covers general-purpose inch pipe threads: NPT is a taper thread with a 60° thread form that seals on the threads, and NPSM is a straight (parallel) thread for free-fitting mechanical joints that does not seal on the thread.

SAE J514 and ISO 8434-2 cover 37° flared tube and hose fittings (JIC): the male 37° flare seats metal to metal against the 37° cone of the female swivel nut, and thread sizes are given by dash number, where each dash is one sixteenth of an inch (-04 is 4/16 in, or 1/4 in).
ISO 8434-1 (the successor to DIN 2353) covers 24° cone compression tube fittings in the light (L) series and the heavy (S) series, sized by tube outside diameter in millimetres.

316L is the low-carbon grade of 316 austenitic stainless steel (carbon 0.03 % maximum), which is why it can be welded without carbide precipitation at the grain boundaries; it contains molybdenum for resistance to chloride pitting.
